chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Mutawakkil (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Adheena, from Muhammad ibn Hukaym, from Maymun al-Baan, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

when he was asked about the saying of Him, Exalted and Glorious is He: «He is the First and the Last». He said: The First, not (in the sense) of a first before Him, nor of a beginning that preceded Him, and the Last, not (in the sense) of an end, as is conceivable about the characteristics of creatures. Rather, (He is) Ancient; a First and a Last, has not perished nor does perish, with no beginning nor end. No incidence occurs upon Him, nor does He change from one condition to another condition, the Creator of everything.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'He is the First and the Last' in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that 'The First' and 'The Last' are not relative temporal markers as understood in created beings, but denote God's absolute eternity without beginning or end. This interpretation safeguards the divine attribute of immutability (*Thabat*), affirming that He is neither subject to change nor confined by the limitations of time, thereby establishing His unique status as the Creator distinct from creation.
